cards.front: Recall a key point about Fabric Printing and Dyeing
cards.back: Block printing uses carved stamps applied to fabric; screen printing forces ink through a mesh stencil — both can create repeat patterns.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Fabric Printing and Dyeing
cards.back: Batik applies wax as a resist before dyeing — the wax blocks dye, creating patterns where the wax is removed.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Fabric Printing and Dyeing
cards.back: Tie-dye and shibori create patterns through resist: binding, folding, twisting or compressing fabric before dyeing.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Fabric Printing and Dyeing
cards.back: Repeat patterns use a single motif repeated systematically — half-drop, brick, mirror and random repeats create different visual effects.

cards.front: What should you know about textile design exam tips?
cards.back: Show the BLOCK/SCREEN alongside the printed fabric. Document the FULL PROCESS — preparation, printing, fixing, washing. Annotate with technique names and specialist vocabulary.

Students often make mistakes with this topic. Wrong: Fabric printing is just stamping paint onto fabric — it is simple and does not need planning. Correct: Successful fabric printing requires careful planning: design the motif, consider the repeat system, choose appropriate fabric (natural fibres for dye, tight weave for screen printing), mix the right consistency of ink/dye, and plan registration

Create printed and dyed fabric samples using at least two different techniques. Design a repeat pattern and print it. Annotate your process explaining your design decisions, technical choices and results.

cards.front: Assessment Objective Focus: Fabric Printing and Dyeing
cards.back: AO1 — Knowledge: Demonstrate knowledge of Fabric Printing and Dyeing using appropriate art vocabulary. Identify techniques, materials and processes accurately.

cards.front: Understanding Fabric Printing and Dyeing in Context
cards.back: Fabric Printing and Dyeing is a fundamental aspect of GCSE Art and Design that connects to all four AQA assessment objectives. Understanding this topic requires both practical skill and contextual knowledge — you must apply techniques effectively AND explain how your work relates to other artists and designers. For fabric printing and dyeing, effective experimentation means testing multiple approaches systematically. Start by researching how professional artists approach fabric printing and dyeing, replicate their techniques as studies, then adapt and combine approaches to develop your own method.
